actions.description: Select one configured multiplexer input source. Selecting OFF stops forwarding and makes the timer publish zero commands; selecting a motion source can immediately re-publish that source's cached last command.

inputs.description: Configured multiplexer source name; OFF selects the zero-command branch
inputs.name: source

actions.name: select_velocity_source

outputs.description: True when the multiplexer accepted the source name
outputs.name: success

outputs.description: Upstream response message naming the selected source
outputs.name: message

actions.description: Publish one speed and steering-angle command on the teleop multiplexer input. The multiplexer caches it and repeats it at its timer rate only while the teleop source is selected. The receipt confirms transmission to rosbridge, not motion, arrival or stopping.

inputs.description: Forward speed written to twist.linear.x; negative values reverse
inputs.name: speed

inputs.description: Steering angle written to twist.angular.z and copied to drive.steering_angle
inputs.name: steering_angle

actions.name: publish_teleop_velocity

outputs.description: True when rosbridge accepted the topic publication
outputs.name: published

outputs.description: Always false: a publication carries no execution confirmation
outputs.name: confirmed

actions.description: Set the multiplexer velocity source to OFF, making its timer publish zero speed and steering commands. Input-free, acknowledged service call; no input is accepted during the latch.
actions.name: stop_velocity_source

outputs.description: True when the multiplexer acknowledged the OFF source
outputs.name: source_off

facts.text: The control configuration declares four multiplexer inputs (wallfollowing AckermannDriveStamped on cmd_vel/wallfollowing, teleop TwistStamped on cmd_vel/teleop, cacc Twist on cmd_vel/cacc, nav2 Twist on cmd_vel/nav2) and three outputs (cmd_vel_twist Twist, cmd_vel_twist_stamped TwistStamped, cmd_vel_ackermann AckermannDriveStamped).
The multiplexer node starts with current_source_ set to OFF unless initial_source names a configured source, and initializes estop_active_ to false.

The constructor registers the relative toggle_cmd_vel_source (auna_msgs/SetString), get_source_status, get_input_sources and debug_state (std_srvs/Trigger) services, plus the absolute /trigger_emergency_stop (std_srvs/SetBool) and /get_estop_status (std_srvs/Trigger) services, on the multiplexer node.
toggleSourceCallback sets current_source_ to OFF for the literal OFF, accepts a configured input name, and returns success=false with a message for an unknown source.
getSourceStatusCallback sets success=true and returns 'Current source: ' followed by the stored source name.
The publish timer uses the last received message of the selected source, or createZeroAckermann when the source is OFF or has no message, and publishes it on every configured output.
The multiplexer declares publish_rate with a default of 20.0 Hz.
createZeroAckermann sets drive.speed and drive.steering_angle to 0.0.
twist_to_ackermann copies TwistStamped.linear.x to drive.speed and TwistStamped.angular.z to drive.steering_angle.
setupSubscribers creates a TwistStamped subscription for each configured source whose declared type is TwistStamped.
twist_callback stores twist_to_ackermann(msg) in last_received_msgs_ under the source name.
The shipped control parameters set publish_rate 20.0, wheelbase 0.32 and convert_yaw_to_steering_angle false for every cmd_vel_multiplexer_node.
The timer converts the steering angle from a yaw rate with the wheelbase only when convert_yaw_to_steering_angle is true.
The launch reads ROBOT_INDEX (default '0') and INITIAL_SOURCE (default 'OFF') from the environment and builds the namespace robot{ROBOT_INDEX}.

The launch builds param_file from auna_common/config/control/params.yaml and topic_file from auna_common/config/control/topics.yaml, and starts the multiplexer node with that namespace, those files and initial_source.
docker-compose.yml runs cmd_multiplexer_robot1 with ROBOT_INDEX=1 and INITIAL_SOURCE=OFF.
docker-compose.yml's teleop service, in the teleop and manual_control profiles, runs auna_teleoperation keyboard_teleop_hold.
The teleop node declares publish_rate 10.0 and base_namespace robot, creates its first publisher for the namespace robot0 and calls _publish from a timer at publish_rate.
The teleop node publishes on /{namespace}/cmd_vel/teleop as TwistStamped or Twist.
The control panel creates clients for the absolute /trigger_emergency_stop and /get_estop_status and for the namespaced get_source_status, get_input_sources and toggle_cmd_vel_source services.
The F1TENTH vesc.launch.py defines vesc_driver_node (vesc_driver), vesc_to_odom_node and ackermann_to_vesc_node (vesc_ackermann) with its namespace launch configuration.

The race-car Gazebo model loads libgazebo_ros_ackermann_drive.so, declares max_steer 0.6458 rad with the comment that a greater cmd_vel angular z is capped, and declares max_speed 10.0 m/s as the maximum absolute linear speed.
The race-car plugin remaps cmd_vel to cmd_vel_twist and odom to odom.
The shipped race_car model-parameter file records drive max_steer 0.6458 and max_speed 1.5 under robot.plugins.drive.

determinism.notes: Event-driven fake with no wall-clock timer or Gazebo step; placeholder source and command state do not establish trajectory or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free analytic stand-in: it answers the declared multiplexer services and teleop topic but runs no cmd_vel_multiplexer_node, rosbridge, Gazebo, physics or vehicle
the fake does not repeat the cached command at the node's 20 Hz timer; it records only the last publication, so it cannot demonstrate continuous motion or stopping time
the fake does not model the Gazebo ackermann drive plugin's speed, steering, collision, tyre or terrain behaviour; the plugin limits are recorded as source facts
the upstream model-parameter file records 1.5 m/s while the active model.urdf plugin records 10.0 m/s; the package uses the active plugin bound and the example site overlay narrows to 1.5

the absolute /trigger_emergency_stop and /get_estop_status services are not bound because every namespaced multiplexer creates the same absolute names; per-robot stop is the namespaced toggle_cmd_vel_source service
the source-OFF stop is a software source change, not an independent hardware emergency stop; the upstream service acknowledgement does not sense that the simulated vehicle has stopped
selecting a non-OFF source re-publishes the multiplexer's cached last command for that source, so the operator must publish the intended command before selecting the source after a stop
the driver assumes the shipped convert_yaw_to_steering_angle=false configuration; if an operator sets it true, the input angular.z is treated as a yaw rate and is converted to a steering angle

speed and steering are operator_required: the plugin's absolute 10.0 m/s and 0.6458 rad are clamps the simulator applies, not a stated command envelope; the example overlay uses 1.5 m/s and 0.6458 rad

the shipped keyboard teleop (docker-compose teleop and manual_control profiles) publishes /robotN/cmd_vel/teleop at 10 Hz on the namespace it selects, overwriting this package's cached teleop command; the nav2, wallfollowing and CACC nodes publish the other inputs
any client of toggle_cmd_vel_source (the RViz control panel, another rosbridge client) can re-select a source while the MHS latch is held; the fake has no other client

the clone also ships an F1TENTH platform launch with a VESC motor driver; nothing in the clone connects the multiplexer's cmd_vel_ackermann output to it, but a deployment that remaps it would drive a real car through this package

measures.description: Read the multiplexer's stored current velocity source through its Trigger service
measures.name: read_velocity_source

operator_required.name: publish_teleop_velocity
operator_required.reason: no command envelope is stated: the race-car plugin clamps the absolute speed at 10.0 m/s and race_car.yaml records 1.5; the operator sets the site speed range

operator_required.name: publish_teleop_velocity
operator_required.reason: no command envelope is stated: the race-car plugin clamps the absolute steering angle at 0.6458 rad; the operator sets the site steering range

safe_state.description: The multiplexer velocity source is set to OFF and its timer publishes zero speed and steering commands on cmd_vel_twist; the service acknowledgement is not sensed vehicle quiescence, the cached source message is retained, and re-selecting a source re-publishes the cached command. Any client of toggle_cmd_vel_source, such as the control panel, can re-select a source while MHS is latched.
